reason: The text depicts the Hebrew people (עם - am) collectively seeking permission to sacrifice to Yahweh in the wilderness. Moses and Aaron negotiate with Pharaoh to allow the Israelites to depart for three days to sacrifice to their God. The repeated phrase 'וְנִזְבְּחָה לַיהוָה אֱלֹהֵינוּ' (we will sacrifice to Yahweh our God) uses the plural first-person, indicating the entire community would participate in sacrifice. The text presents no restriction limiting sacrifice exclusively to priests. This passage precedes the formal establishment of the Aaronic priesthood and Temple sacrificial system detailed in Leviticus.
